claims.statement: Lean theorem NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 (NavierStokes/ComparatorSolution.lean, over the solution-side definitions of NavierStokes/ComparatorDefinitions.lean): for every nu > 0 there are a smooth, divergence-free, rapidly decaying u0 : R^3 -> R^3 and a smooth, rapidly decaying force f such that no pair (v, p) of smooth functions on R^3 x [0,infty) satisfies the Navier-Stokes equations with data (nu, u0, f), the divergence-free condition, the initial condition and bounded energy. Our own #print axioms audit file (SolutionAudit_NS.lean, rc 0) reports exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; the module was rebuilt from source and all 53,752 declarations of its closure re-passed the kernel (replay log hashed here). A statement about the Lean term only.

Lean theorem NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic: for every nu > 0 there are smooth, divergence-free, 1-periodic data u0 and a smooth 1-periodic force f with time decay such that no pair (v, p) of smooth functions on R^3 x [0,infty), with v and p 1-periodic in space, satisfies the equations with data (nu, u0, f), the divergence-free condition and the initial condition. Same audit file, same axioms, same replay as A-0001. A statement about the Lean term only (the periodic pressure is a field of the solution class; see C-0003).

Lean theorem Euler.euler_breakdown_R3 (Euler/Solution.lean): there is a smooth, divergence-free, rapidly decaying u0 : R^3 -> R^3 such that no triple (v, p) satisfies the incompressible Euler existence-and-smoothness class EulerExistenceAndSmoothnessR3 (smooth, bounded energy) for u0. Our own audit file SolutionAudit_Euler.lean (rc 0) reports exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; all 34,648 declarations of the closure re-passed the kernel (replay log hashed here). A statement about the Lean term only.

Lean theorem Euler.exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity (Euler/Solution.lean): a supplementary statement for compactly supported smooth divergence-free initial velocity on R^3 in a Sobolev solution class on [0,T*), with a Beale-Kato-Majda-type divergence of the time integral of the vorticity sup norm. Same audit file, axioms and replay as A-0003. A statement about the Lean term only; we did not audit its solution class against a literature source.

Fefferman's official statement of the Clay problem: 'we ask for a proof of one of the following four statements' (A), (B), (C), (D); (C) Breakdown of Navier-Stokes solutions on R^3 and (D) Breakdown on R^3/Z^3 are the two negative alternatives, as quoted.
The Clay errata appended to the problem description: 'The further condition p(x + e_j, t) = p(x, t) should be made explicit in Eqn (8).'

Fefferman on the Euler equations: 'These problems are also open and very important for the Euler equations (nu = 0), although the Euler equation is not on the Clay Institute's list of prize problems.'

The corpus README (openai/NavierStokesAndEuler at f9e8bc5b) describes its results as the two Navier-Stokes results for every positive viscosity, named as alternatives (C) and (D) of the Clay description, and a smooth compactly supported divergence-free Euler initial velocity whose unforced solution develops a singularity in finite time. This records what the corpus authors claim, not that it holds.

Scope. We independently rebuilt and audited the openai/NavierStokesAndEuler Lean corpus (rebuild, axioms, soundness-escape scans, kernel replay, elaborated-statement identity, a second statement-fidelity reading). This is not a claim that a Clay problem is solved, and not a verification that the mathematics of the proof is correct beyond what the checks in this paper establish. Credit for the proofs belongs to the corpus authors; the Clay Institute's own process decides any prize.

Fidelity of (C): a field-by-field reading (FIDELITY2.md, written before reading H9) of Fefferman's (C) against the Lean statement navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 and the definitions it is stated over found no mismatch: nu > 0 universally quantified; u0 smooth, divergence-free with (4); f smooth on R^3 x [0,infty) with (5); no solution (v,p) of (1), (2), (3), (6), (7), with the solution class carrying no extra restriction, and (7) encoded as MemLp together with a uniform energy bound. A judgement of statement fidelity by an AI agent, not a person. The witness uses zero initial data and a nonzero force, which (C) allows; (C) is not the negation of (A), which takes f = 0.

Fidelity of (D): the Lean statement navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic matches Fefferman's (D) as corrected by the Clay errata, with one interpretive caveat: it requires the pressure to be 1-periodic as a field of the solution class. This shrinks the class of admissible solutions, so nonexistence is weaker than nonexistence read against the main text alone (without periodic pressure, p = -g(t).x with a spatially constant flow is a classical non-uniqueness device). The errata attaches the condition to Eqn (8), the data hypotheses, although p is an unknown; reading it as a condition on accepted solutions is the only coherent reading we found. Judgement of an AI agent.

Euler: euler_breakdown_R3 is the (C)-type statement with nu = 0 and f = 0 (conditions (1) with nu = 0 and f = 0, (2), (3), (4), (6), (7)); the Euler equations are not on the Clay list. exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity has no Clay counterpart and is reported only as a Lean statement; its BKM-type clause matches the form of the Beale-Kato-Majda remark of the PDF, and its solution class was read but not audited against a literature source.

Implication, conditional and not a Clay determination: if the Lean statement of (C) is a faithful formalization of Fefferman's (C) (a human judgement, C-0002), and if the Lean 4.34.0-rc2 kernel, the toolchain and the reused Mathlib are sound, then the kernel-checked theorem navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 is a formal proof of Fefferman's alternative (C). This is not a Clay determination: the Clay Institute's own process decides whether anything is a solution and whether any prize is due. Nothing in this paper says the problem is solved, or that the mathematics has been refereed by people.

Why #print axioms alone is insufficient (a demonstration of a known limitation of axiom printing, not a new vulnerability): (1) Lean's addDecl run under set_option debug.skipKernelTC true stores a declaration without kernel type checking; (2) the .olean serializes it; (3) an importing file trusts the stored declaration; (4) #print axioms walks constant references only, and the forged proof True.intro of False references no axiom; (5) only a replay that re-runs the kernel on the stored declarations compares the stored type with the stored value and rejects it. Hence the axiom verdict (A-0001..A-0004) is to be read together with the kernel replay and with the source scan, which finds no skipKernelTC, addDecl, or set_option in the corpus. The observation on the planted module is X-0004.

What is not established: (i) Comparator, lean4export and nanoda were not run (the Comparator require was removed from the build copy and is absent from the prebuilt package set; the Comparator build on this machine targets Lean 4.34.1 while the corpus pins 4.34.0-rc2; nanoda is not installed); the kernel replay and leanchecker use the same Lean kernel through the same Lean.Replay mechanism, so they are a second driver of one kernel, not an independent kernel; (ii) Mathlib 85e3a25e and its dependencies were reused and trusted, neither rebuilt nor replayed; (iii) the diff of the challenge file against google-deepmind/formal-conjectures@8bf45ed (and whether the pinned openai/NavierStokesAndEuler@8937a8f referred to by the upstream index equals f9e8bc5b) was not done; (iv) the mathematics of the proof was not refereed by people by us, and the natural-language papers were not checked; statement identity is checked against the corpus's challenge file and statement fidelity is judged against Fefferman's text, not against OpenAI's natural-language papers, and no claim is made that the Lean statements or development match those papers (clarified in v1.2); (v) the Lean kernel and toolchain are trusted; (vi) statement fidelity is a human judgement, made here by AI agents, and no person has audited any statement.

Limitations of the audit itself: one AI agent instance rebuilt and audited, another wrote the fidelity table blind to H9, and a third (this paper stage) wrote the paper from the saved logs without re-running any check; all are instances of one pipeline. The planted controls show that each layer can reject what it is designed to reject; they do not show that no other kind of escape exists. The rebuild ran at machine contention (an unrelated Lean job ran concurrently), so wall times are not benchmarks. No human has reviewed the work.

Rebuild from source at HEAD f9e8bc5b (tree clean) with Lean 4.34.0-rc2 and the corpus's lakefile options: 609 modules of the NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution closure (rc 0, 'Build completed successfully (9371 jobs)', 3,300 s), 1,829 modules of Euler.Solution (rc 0, 10591 jobs, 5,109 s), the 2 ComparatorChallenges modules (rc 0, 4 intentional sorry warnings); 2,440 .olean files; zero warnings and zero errors in the two solution builds; Mathlib reused (0 'Built Mathlib' lines). One build-only lakefile change: the Comparator require and two manifest entries removed in the build copy.

Source scan (scripts/source_scan.py, comments stripped, strings blanked) of the 2,585-module closure and of all 2,659 corpus .lean files: 0 code hits for sorry-in-solutions, admit, native_decide, ofReduceBool/trustCompiler, axiom, implemented_by, extern, unsafe, csimp, opaque, partial, #exit, set_option of any kind, debug.*, skipKernelTC, addDecl/modifyEnv/setEnv, #eval/run_cmd/initialize, import Lean, command_elab attributes; 4 sorry hits, all placeholders of ComparatorChallenges (not imported by either solution). The pattern group elab/macro/syntax matches 150 (closure) and 156 (all files) lines, all of them 'local notation' (148 / 154) or @[inherit_doc] (2 / 2); no file starts a line with elab, macro, syntax or macro_rules. attribute [local instance]: 10 (closure), 11 (all files). Planted controls: every category caught on a scratch copy; unmodified copy clean.

Environment scan (soundnessScan in lean_scripts/DumpCore.lean.txt, run inside the built environment): the proof closure of NS has 93,597 constants (31,516 from 597 corpus modules) and of Euler 94,411 (26,213 from 1,756 corpus modules); the only axioms in either closure are propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice; no ofReduceBool, ofReduceNat, trustCompiler or sorryAx; no flagged constant from a corpus module (the flags are core extern/implemented_by/opaque and Mathlib irreducible_def wrappers); the corpus adds no axiom to the 15 that core declares; 12 (NS) and 39 (Euler) corpus _unsafe_rec compiler auxiliaries exist in the environment, none in a proof closure. Planted controls (axiom, native_decide auxiliary axiom, implemented_by, sorryAx, unsafe, partial, extern) all flagged.

Planted forged declaration (controls/forged/src/A2Forged.lean): False 'proved' by True.intro, added with addDecl under debug.skipKernelTC. It compiles; a theorem using it prints 'does not depend on any axioms' under #print axioms; #check from a fresh importing file succeeds. leanchecker A2Forged exits 1 and A2Replay.lean exits 1 with '(kernel) declaration type mismatch, A2Forged.forged_false has type True but it is expected to have type False'. The positive control (NavierStokes.ComparatorDefinitions, 95 declarations) replays OK.

Kernel replay of the whole corpus (A2Replay.lean, Lean.Replay, one shared base environment of 774,999 Mathlib-side constants): NS closure 609 modules, 53,752 declarations, 'REPLAY OK' in 621,964 ms (wall 11:33, max RSS 8.1 GB); Euler closure 1,829 modules, 34,648 declarations, 'REPLAY OK' in 933,056 ms (wall 15:42, max RSS 9.8 GB). Two corpus declarations per closure (the congr_simp lemmas HasDerivWithinAt/HasDerivAt and compLpL/compLeftContinuous) already exist in Mathlib with identical type hashes. Lean.Replay skips by design the 51 compiler-generated _unsafe_rec auxiliaries (12 NS, 39 Euler; none in any proof closure) and the 4 identical congr_simp duplicates; the auditor's independent replay attributes 53,750 / 34,646 constants to corpus modules (the 2 congr_simp per closure belong to Mathlib modules).

leanchecker of the v4.34.0-rc2 toolchain on 8 modules (NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution, ComparatorR3Theorem, ComparatorTheorem, ComparatorDefinitions, Euler.Solution, Euler.SolutionDefinitions, ComparatorChallenges.NavierStokes, ComparatorChallenges.Euler): all rc 0, 15-17 s each. The challenge modules pass because sorryAx is a legitimate kernel axiom; the axiom check, not the kernel, rejects sorry. leanchecker without --fresh checks only the named module's own declarations against its imports; a forged lemma in an imported module would pass it (auditor control), so closure coverage rests on the full replay (X-0005).

Elaborated-statement identity: the transitive statement closure (types of all constants, values of definitions and opaques; not theorem proofs) of the two root theorems has 5,599 constants (NS) and 5,521 (Euler) in the reference environment (verbatim ComparatorChallenges file + dump) and in the solution environment; 0 only on either side, 0 differing after normalising the module component of hygienic binder names (alpha-renaming); 23 (NS) and 25 (Euler) corpus constants also compared as full Expr text. Raw differences before normalisation (4 NS constructor types; 3 Euler constants) have equal Expr.hash. Negative control: changing < E to <= E in the reference gives 1 differing constant (NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn.mk). Expr.hash is used for non-corpus constants.

Planted #print axioms controls (controls/env/EnvControl.lean): a sorry (reports sorryAx), a smuggled axiom (reports the axiom), and native_decide proving a false equation through implemented_by (reports an auxiliary ..._native.native_decide.ax_1_1 axiom, not Lean.ofReduceBool, on 4.34.0-rc2); each is outside the whitelist and is caught.

Semantics probes compiled against the pinned Mathlib (audit/Semantics.lean, Semantics2.lean): the notation infinity under open ContDiff elaborates to WithTop.some (top : NatENat), not the analytic omega ('example : (infinity : WithTop NatENat) != omega := by decide' and an rfl example compile); the Laplacian on R^3 -> R^3 is instLaplacian and equals the sum over an orthonormal basis of D^2 w(x)[e_i,e_i] (an example using laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis compiles); gradient is the Riesz representative of fderiv; the norm on R^3 x R is the max (rfl). One #check line of Semantics.lean uses a name that does not exist (InnerProductSpace.laplacian) and reports an unknown-identifier error; the assertions are the example lines, none of which errors.

Comparison of the two statement audits: FIDELITY2.md (written before reading H9) and H9 AUDIT.md (2026-10-25) agree on every row of (C) (all MATCH) and on (D) (matches the errata-corrected text; the periodic-pressure caveat); no disagreement on any row. H9's open caveats 4 (Mathlib version) and 6 (does the solution prove this exact statement) are addressed by X-0009 and X-0007; the diff against formal-conjectures@8bf45ed remains open in both.
